question.text: One mole of $\mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$ and two moles of $\mathrm{SO}_{2(\mathrm{~g})}$ were heated in a closed vessel of one-litre capacity at $1098 \mathrm{~K}$. At equilibrium $1.6$ moles of $\mathrm{SO}_{3(\mathrm{~g})}$ were found. The equilibrium constant $K_c$ of the reaction would be

solution.text:
$\quad \mathrm{O}_2+2 \mathrm{SO}_2 \rightleftharpoons 2 \mathrm{SO}_3$ at $\mathrm{t}=0 \quad 1 \quad 2 \quad 0$ at equil. $(1-\alpha) 2(1-\alpha) \quad 2 \alpha$ Given at equilibrium
$$
\begin{aligned}
& 2 \alpha=1.6 \\
& K_{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{(2 \alpha)^2}{(1-\alpha)(2-2 \alpha)^2}=\frac{\begin{array}{c}
\alpha=0.8 \\
(0.8)^2
\end{array}}{(1-0.8)(1-0.8)^2} \\
& =\frac{0.64}{0.002} \\
& K_{\mathrm{C}}=80 \\
&
\end{aligned}
$$
